The difference between writing code and owning a system

ENGINEERING · 7 MIN READ · SEPTEMBER 2026

Writing code gives a system a capability. Owning it means accepting responsibility for what happens next.

A feature can be correct when it leaves your editor and still create problems in production. Deployments can fail. Dependencies can behave differently. A database can become the bottleneck. An alert can be misleading. Someone can get paged at two in the morning without knowing what to do.

That is why I think about engineering ownership as a larger loop: build → deploy → observe → operate → learn → improve.

Documentation is part of that loop. Runbooks are part of it. Monitoring is part of it. Incident response is part of it.

The code is still important. But the code is only one part of the system an engineer is responsible for.
